newsitem.title: USA: Alyeska pump sta. fire slows pipeline throughput.
newsitem.headline: Alyeska pump sta. fire slows pipeline throughput.

text.p: A small explosion and resulting fire at the trans-Alaska pipeline's Prudhoe Bay pump station caused in interruption in oil flow, the system's operator said Thursday.
No injuries occurred in the 0620 local/1420 GMT accident, said Alyeska Pipeline Service Co, the consortium that operates the pipeline
The fire, which flared in a generator at the pump station, was doused by hand-held fire extinguishers, Alyeska said. Its cause was under investigation, the company said.

Pipeline throughput was slowed to a rate of 770,000 barrels a day, from the normal rate of 1.2 million to 1.3 million barrels a day, until a back-up generator was put into use, Alyeska said. The slowdown lasted for only 35 minutes, and there was no impact on North Slope oil producers, Alyeska said.
Alyeska operates the 800-mile oil line and its Alyeska terminal.
Major owners of the consortium are British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield and Exxon. Unocal, Phillips Petroleum, Mobil and Amerada Hess own minor shares.
